footnotes: From pre-tax income to net income to Diamondback: includes $117M of losses allocated to noncontrolling interests; after $8.0M of preferred dividends. The filing reports no separate capital expenditures, so free cash flow equals operating cash flow.

Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC (income statement lines as the filing presents them); free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditures. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue rose 35.8% to $15.0B in 2025. Operating income fell 71.2% to $1.3B, a 8.4% margin.
Net income fell 50.1% to $1.7B, or $5.73 per share. Operating cash flow was $8.8B and free cash flow $8.8B, versus $6.4B; Diamondback returned $1.2B through dividends.
sources: Diamondback Energy, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)

spotlights.cap: Net income was $1.7B, or $5.73 per share.

risks: The nature of our business activities subjects us to certain hazards and risks
Geopolitics and market conditions for oil and natural gas, and particularly volatility in prices for oil and natural gas…
Our commodity price derivatives could result in financial losses, may fail to protect us from declines in commodity prices…
Changes in U.S. trade policy and the impact of tariffs may have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations
strategy: Focus on low cost development and continuous operational improvement
Continue to deliver on our capital return program
Leverage our experience operating in the Permian Basin
